## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}
library(phangorn)
library(phytools)
tree_file <- "/Users/kylewillard/Downloads/Adelphi/MastersThesis/Seymour et al 2026 Supplemental Code/Phylogeny/Scaled Supertree.tre"
tree <- read.tree(tree_file)
plot(tree)
```

```{r}
library(geiger)
trait_data <- read.csv("~/Downloads/Adelphi/MastersThesis/Seymour et al 2026 Supplemental Code/PGLS Data/All Clades-Table 1.csv")
rownames(trait_data) <- trait_data$Taxon
chk<-name.check(tree, trait_data)
chk
```

```{r}
library(ape)
library(nlme)
library(caper)
bm <- corBrownian(1, tree, form = ~ Taxon)
bm
pgls<-gls(LOG.Qdot..ml.min. ~ LOG.Body.mass..kg., data=trait_data, correlation=bm)
summary(pgls)
pgls
plot(LOG.Qdot..ml.min. ~ LOG.Body.mass..kg., data=trait_data, main ="Log Body Mass(kg) vs Log Blood Flow (Qdot) in Amniotes")
abline(pgls, col ="red")
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r}
resids <- residuals(pgls, type = "response")
resids_vector <- setNames(resids, rownames(trait_data))
resid_map <- contMap(tree, resids_vector, plot = FALSE)
resid_map <- setMap(resid_map, colors = c("blue", "white", "red"))
plot(resid_map, 
     fsize = 0.8, 
     lwd = 3, 
     leg.txt = "Phylogenetic Residuals")
```
